blocks.explanation:
\(y\) ki series 1 ke baghair shuru hoti hai. Agar dono taraf 1 jama kar dein to \(1 + y\) poori binomial series ban jati hai.
Saabit kya karna hai? \(y^{2} + 2y - 2 = 0\).
Rule kaunsa? Series ko \((1 + x)^{n}\) maan kar \(n\), \(x\) dhoondna.
Plan: Doosri aur teesri term ko \(nx\) aur \(\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}x^{2}\) se milayenge; do equations se \(n\) aur \(x\) mil jayenge. Phir jama, phir \(y\), phir equation mein rakhna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1 \cdot 3}{2!}(\frac{1}{3})^{2} + \frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3!}(\frac{1}{3})^{3} + \dots\)
Saabit karna hai: \(y^{2} + 2y - 2 = 0\).
Tareeqa: Dono taraf 1 jama karenge; \(1 + y\) kisi \((1 + x)^{n}\) ki expansion hogi. Doosri aur teesri term ko \(nx\) aur \(\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}x^{2}\) se milayenge; do equations se \(n\) aur \(x\) mil jayenge.

1 jama karein
\[1 + y = 1 + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1 \cdot 3}{2!}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{2} + \dots\]
Kyun: Har binomial series 1 se shuru hoti hai. Yeh 1 di gayi series mein nahi tha, is liye khud jama kiya taa ke shakal poori ho jaye.
Dhyan dein: aakhir mein jama ko \(1 + y\) ke barabar rakhna hai, \(y\) ke barabar nahi. Yeh 1 bhool jana aam ghalti hai.

Do equations
\[nx = \dfrac{1}{3} \quad (1)\]
\[\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2}x^{2} = \dfrac{3}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{1}{6} \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Doosri term \(\tfrac{1}{3}\) aur teesri term \(\tfrac{1 \cdot 3}{2!} \cdot \tfrac{1}{9} = \tfrac{1}{6}\) ko general terms ke barabar rakha.

\(n\) aur \(x\) nikalein
\[\dfrac{n(n - 1)x^{2}}{(nx)^{2}} = \dfrac{1/3}{1/9} = 3\]
\[\dfrac{n - 1}{n} = 3 \Rightarrow n = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[x = \dfrac{1/3}{-1/2} = -\dfrac{2}{3}\]
Kyun: (2) ko 2 se multiply kar ke \(n(n - 1)x^{2} = \tfrac{1}{3}\) bana, phir (1) ke square \(\tfrac{1}{9}\) se divide kiya. \(n - 1 = 3n\) se \(n = -\tfrac{1}{2}\). Phir (1) se \(x = \tfrac{1}{3} \div (-\tfrac{1}{2}) = -\tfrac{2}{3}\).

Chauthi term se tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{(-\frac{1}{2})(-\frac{3}{2})(-\frac{5}{2})}{6}\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{3}\]
\[= \left(-\dfrac{5}{16}\right)\left(-\dfrac{8}{27}\right) = \dfrac{5}{54}\]
\[\dfrac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3!} \cdot \dfrac{1}{27} = \dfrac{15}{162} = \dfrac{5}{54}\ \checkmark\]
Kyun: Agli term bhi mil gayi, to \(n = -\tfrac{1}{2}\), \(x = -\tfrac{2}{3}\) pakke hain.

Jama
\[1 + y = \left(1 - \dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{-1/2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{-1/2}\]
\[= \sqrt{3}\]
\[y = \sqrt{3} - 1\]
Kyun: \(|x| = \tfrac{2}{3} < 1\), series converge karti hai. \((\tfrac{1}{3})^{-1/2} = 3^{1/2} = \sqrt{3}\). Phir 1 wapas minus kiya.

Equation saabit karein
\[y + 1 = \sqrt{3}\]
\[(y + 1)^{2} = 3\]
\[y^{2} + 2y + 1 = 3\]
\[y^{2} + 2y - 2 = 0\]
Kyun: Root hatane ke liye dono taraf square kiya. \((y + 1)^{2} = y^{2} + 2y + 1\). Phir 3 ko left par laya: \(1 - 3 = -2\). Yahi saabit karna tha.
blocks.final_answer: \(1 + y = \left(1 - \frac{2}{3}\right)^{-1/2} = \sqrt{3}\), is liye \(y^{2} + 2y - 2 = 0\). Saabit ho gaya.
